provenance.instrument: West Brandywine Township Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 200 Zoning, adopted 9-6-1984, as amended) and Chapter 89 Flood Damage Prevention (Ord. No. 2017-03 of 9-21-2017), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 WE1756, Township of West Brandywine, linked from the township's Codes and Zoning page. The flood ordinance's deed notice names 'West Brandywine Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania' (89-802I), so this is West Brandywine township, Chester County. District use lists and area and bulk rules are text. The zoning attachments are diagrams (building line, dwelling classifications, parking lot, yard calculations, visibility). New Laws: none (0)
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 05-21-2026.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.' 200-14 and 200-19 carry Ord. No. 2026-03 of 3-5-2026
checks: The ADU is a use of a 'country property': 'Accessory dwelling unit not exceeding 1,500 square feet in gross floor area, whether in the same structure as the principal residence or in a traditional outbuilding (such as a barn, stable, carriage house, or spring house)'. It needs conditional use approval by the Board of Supervisors on a lot of at least 10 acres that is restricted from subdivision into parcels under 10 acres, and the approval ends if such a subdivision is later approved (200-15B(3)). Country properties are a conditional use in R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, RM and LI (200-14C(8), 200-19C(7), 200-23C(6), 200-28C(4), 200-37C(14), 200-44C(4)), and in L-2, which permits every use of R-2 (200-32A). MSI does not list them (200-50)

One ADU on a lot of 10 acres or more in gross tract area, and one more for each additional 25 acres. The unit is designed to harmonize with vernacular rural buildings in the township's historic landscape, and it may not be subdivided off unless every resulting lot complies with the chapter (200-15B(3))

The definition says country properties are 'Properties exceeding 10 acres in gross' area (1-20 'Country properties'), while 200-15B(3) allows the unit on a lot 'greater than or equal to 10 acres'. A lot of exactly 10 acres is not settled

Residential conversion of a detached building or farm building is a special exception in R-2, R-3 and R-4, and in L-2 through R-2 (200-19B(1), 200-23B(1), 200-28B(1), 200-32A). The lot is listed as 'Minimum lot area per use/unit': 3 acres in R-2 and L-2, 2 acres in R-3 and R-4 (200-20B(1)(b), 200-24B(1)(b), 200-29B(1)(a), 200-33A). Its standards (200-84) speak of converting a single-family dwelling into more units: each unit at least 800 sq ft, 'The yard and building area requirements for the district in which the dwelling is located shall apply to each dwelling unit', no outside change other than safety measures, separate entrances, kitchens and baths, County Health Department sewer and water, and the Zoning Hearing Board sets the number of families. Read with 200-84B, the lot figure may be per unit: 6 acres for two units in R-2 and L-2, 4 acres in R-3 and R-4. The Planning Commission gives an advisory review of any special exception (200-151)

Tenant farm dwellings accessory to the principal farmhouse meet the residential area and bulk rules of 200-16. Agriculture needs a tract of at least four acres, and on a farm all dwellings and buildings stand at least 50 ft from all property lines (200-15A(1), (3), (5)). Housing for farm workers is a special exception in R-1 (200-14B(2), 200-86): it stays accessory on a tract qualified as agriculture, takes at most 10% of the tract or five acres, whichever is less, at most three units an acre, and needs DEP approval for seasonal farm labor camps

Two-family and multiple-family dwellings are possible only in the open space design option, a conditional use (200-14C(2), 200-19C(2), 200-23C(2), 200-28C(1), Article XXII, not read). Two-family dwellings were removed from R-3 in 1994 (200-23A editor's note)

Accessory buildings stand in side or rear yards (front yards only on corner lots, and not in the required front yard). Under 400 sq ft: 10 ft from side and rear lines. Over 400 sq ft of footprint: 20 ft. At most 25 ft tall, and at most 20% of any required yard. Accessory uses 'shall not be conducted as an independent principal use' (200-83A, C). The height exemption for barns reaches only structures 'not devoted to human occupancy' (200-82), so a barn with a dwelling unit takes the 25 ft height. For uses by special exception or conditional use, R-1, R-2 and L-2 set side, front and rear yards of 50 ft each (200-16B, 200-20B, 200-33A). The ADU is a conditional use, so these yards are read as binding it there

Front yards are 80 ft on Routes 322 and 82 and 60 ft on collector roads (Cedar Knoll, Reeceville, Hibernia, Springton, Swinehart, Little Washington Lyndell), in place of the district front yard (200-80)

Coverage: each district sets a building coverage and a total lot coverage. Lot coverage is 'The percentage of net lot area or net tract area, as applicable, which is covered by all buildings and structures and impervious surfaces' (1-20 'Lot coverage'). Net lot area leaves out the floodplain, wetlands, the Severe Slope District, hydric soils, and 75% of land within 50 ft of the top of a stream bank and of the Moderate Slope District (1-20 'Lot area, net'). Lots on on-site sewage need a contiguous net area of 33,000 sq ft clear of street rights-of-way, the floodplain, wetlands and the Severe Slope District (200-16C and the like)

Floodplain (Chapter 89): in any identified floodplain area only the uses of 89-501D and E are permitted, agriculture 'excluding structures', recreation, yards and nonstructural accessory uses among them, and 'With the exception of § 89-501D and E above, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' (89-501D, 89-502). 'All structures with the exception of those specifically allowed in § 200-61A and B' are a prohibited activity, and 'No variance shall be granted for prohibited activities' (89-601A(2), 89-802B). 200-61 is reserved, and 89-502 and 89-802I speak of a variance for new construction or the erection of a structure. On a contiguous lot no structure less than 25 ft from the floodplain boundary, and no building, structure or drainage field within 50 ft of a special flood hazard area where the zoning setback is less (89-501D(3), (4)). In a floodway no new construction without a DEP permit. In AE zones without a floodway no new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank without a DEP permit. In an A zone the township may require the lowest floor 3 ft above the highest adjacent grade, and fully enclosed space below the lowest floor is prohibited (89-402B, 89-402C(1), 89-502C(1))

Steep Slope District (Article XIII, an overlay): in the Severe Slope District (over 25%) 'Structures other than those specified as a permitted use or special exception' are prohibited, and only the yard of a dwelling outside the district is permitted there (200-72A(2), 200-73C). In the Moderate Slope District (15% to 25%) 'Residential development contingent upon approval of Board of Supervisors as advised by the Township Engineer' (200-72A(1)(c)). Density one dwelling unit per two acres, building coverage 5%, impervious cover 10% (moderate) or 6% (severe) (200-74)
Variances: Zoning Hearing Board on unnecessary hardship (200-145). No bar on a use variance was found

Density: in R-1 'the maximum number of lots or dwelling units permitted on any tract shall be calculated by multiplying the net tract area times 0.5', and 0.8 in R-2 (200-16A(9), 200-20A(9)). Whether an ADU counts as a dwelling unit there is not settled. On a lot of 10 acres or more it seldom binds

Woodlands and riparian buffers: a building permit applicant meets the subdivision ordinance rules (167-64, 167-65, not read). On a lot of record the Zoning Officer may allow intrusion limited 'to the minimum practicable extent necessary' (200-100D). A grading permit is needed when new impervious cover plus disturbance exceeds 10% of the lot or 5,000 sq ft, whichever is less (200-88A(1)(c))

Nonconforming lots: a lot held in single and separate ownership at the chapter's effective date that is below the minimum may be built on. A variance is needed for any building when the setbacks cannot be met, and adjacent land of the same owner must be combined first (200-135)

Some district sections still refer to the Flood Plain District of Article XII (200-16C and the like), and 200-9 still lists the FP and PW districts. Article XII was repealed in 2017 (floodplain now Chapter 89) and is now the General Commercial Overlay, and Article XXIV is reserved

RM permits single-family dwellings by right and two-family and multiple-family dwellings by conditional use in a planned mixed use development or in a Class I or Class II historic structure, where the Board may vary area and bulk rules (200-37A(8), C(4), C(5)). LI lists no dwelling, so a house there is nonconforming (200-44)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: West Brandywine Township Codes and Zoning. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-18: Articles IV to VII, Article XIV (200-77 to 200-96), 200-145 and 200-146, and 89-402, 89-601 and 89-802 of Chapter 89, with code searches. Second reading on 2026-11-18: Article II and Chapter 1 definitions, Articles VIII to XIII (L-2, RM, LI, MSI, General Commercial Overlay, Steep Slope), XVIII, XXIII, 200-100, 200-101, and 89-501 and 89-502. Not read: Articles XV to XVII, XX to XXII, XXIV, XXV, 200-100.1 to 200-100.6, the rest of Chapter 89, and the zoning map. The ADU text dates from Ord. No. 01-02 of 10-4-2001, used as the effective date.

term.note: 'Accessory dwelling unit not exceeding 1,500 square feet in gross floor area' on a country property

status.note: 'Where approved by the Board of Supervisors as a conditional use, the following uses shall be permitted on country properties'

scope_districts.note: Country properties are a conditional use in these districts. L-2 permits every use of R-2 (200-32A)

status_outside.note: MSI does not list country properties (200-50)

path.note: Board of Supervisors after a hearing under Article XXI

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on unnecessary hardship. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Residential conversion of a detached building or farm building (R-2, L-2)
value.conditions: Each unit at least 800 sq ft. 'The yard and building area requirements for the district in which the dwelling is located shall apply to each dwelling unit', and are not reduced. No outside change other than safety measures, with fire escapes at the rear. The Zoning Hearing Board sets the number of families. Separate entrances, kitchens and baths, firewalls between units, and County Health Department sewer and water. Parking for each unit, four spaces a unit (200-101F). The Planning Commission gives an advisory review (200-151). Side, front and rear yards 50 ft each, building coverage 15%, lot coverage 20% (200-20B, 200-33A)

requires.condition: A building of at least 1,600 sq ft, so two units each have 800 sq ft

value.note: The district lists name a 'detached building or farm building', while 200-84 speaks of converting a single-family dwelling, so both are read as covered

disputed_min_lot.note: The figure is 'Minimum lot area per use/unit', and 200-84B applies the district requirements to each dwelling unit, so two units may need 6 acres

value.name: Residential conversion of a detached building or farm building (R-3, R-4)
value.conditions: Each unit at least 800 sq ft. 'The yard and building area requirements for the district in which the dwelling is located shall apply to each dwelling unit', and are not reduced. No outside change other than safety measures, with fire escapes at the rear. The Zoning Hearing Board sets the number of families. Separate entrances, kitchens and baths, firewalls between units, and County Health Department sewer and water. Parking for each unit, four spaces a unit (200-101F). The Planning Commission gives an advisory review (200-151). In R-3 side yards 20 ft, front 50 ft, rear 40 ft, building coverage 25%. In R-4 the same yards, building coverage 20%, lot coverage 25% (200-24B, 200-29B)

requires.condition: A building of at least 1,600 sq ft, so two units each have 800 sq ft

value.note: The district lists name a 'detached building or farm building', while 200-84 speaks of converting a single-family dwelling, so both are read as covered

disputed_min_lot.note: The figure is 'Minimum lot area per use/unit', and 200-84B applies the district requirements to each dwelling unit, so two units may need 4 acres

value.name: Tenant farm dwelling on a farm (R-1, R-2, R-3, R-4, L-2)
value.conditions: On a tract of at least four acres in agricultural use, a tenant farm dwelling accessory to the principal farmhouse meets the residential area and bulk rules of 200-16. All dwellings and buildings stand at least 50 ft from all property lines, and lot coverage on a farm is at most 15%

requires.condition: The tract is in agricultural use under 200-15
The dwelling houses a tenant farmer and is accessory to the principal farmhouse

value.note: The code names tenant farm dwellings only in the agricultural use rules. It does not say how many, or whether each needs its own 1.5 acres under 200-16

value.name: Conversion of an identified historic resource (Historic Resources Map)
value.conditions: 'An Identified Historic Resource in any zoning district may be converted into two or more dwelling units' by conditional use of the Board of Supervisors after Historical Commission review. The 200-84 conversion standards apply, at most four units in one structure, each with at least 800 sq ft of habitable space. The Board may waive or modify area and bulk requirements to protect the resource, and the approval must be necessary to its preservation. In RM a Class I or Class II historic structure may hold two-family or multiple-family dwellings by conditional use, with area and bulk rules varied by the Board (200-37C(4), (5))

requires.condition: The building is a Class I or Class II historic resource on the township's Historic Resources Map
The Board finds the approval necessary to preserve the historic resource

value.note: It reaches any district, with or without a country property. A historic barn or carriage house may be converted the same way

historic_bypass.note: Article XXIII gives an identified historic resource a conversion path by conditional use (listed as another path). It is not an ADU path and does not lift the country property rules

value.condition: The unit is allowed on 'any legal building lot greater than or equal to 10 acres in gross tract area'. The definition of country properties reads 'Properties exceeding 10 acres in gross' area, so a lot of exactly 10 acres is not settled.

The country property is restricted from subdivision into parcels under 10 acres in gross area, and the owner agrees in the application that the approval ends if such a subdivision is later approved. The unit may not be subdivided off unless every resulting lot complies with the chapter.
The unit is designed to harmonize with vernacular rural buildings in the township's historic landscape.

In any identified floodplain area only the uses of 89-501D and E are permitted, such as agriculture excluding structures, recreation, yards and nonstructural accessory uses, and any new construction or substantial improvement is prohibited. 'All structures' other than those allowed in 200-61A and B are a prohibited activity, and 'No variance shall be granted for prohibited activities'.

no_variance.quote: No variance shall be granted for prohibited activities (Article VI)

disputed_by.note: 89-502 sets rules 'If a variance is obtained for new construction or substantial improvements in the identified floodplain area', 89-802I speaks of a variance 'to permit the erection of a structure in any identified floodplain area', and the 200-61A and B named in 89-601A(2) are reserved

value.condition: In an AE zone without a floodway 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse, unless the appropriate permit is obtained from the Department of Environmental Protection Regional Office'.

On a lot next to an identified floodplain area, no structure may be placed less than 25 ft from the floodplain boundary, and no building, structure or sanitary drainage field within 50 ft of the boundary of a special flood hazard area where the zoning setback for that area is less than 50 ft.

Steep Slope District: in the Severe Slope District (over 25%) no structure other than a permitted use or special exception, and only the yard of a dwelling outside the district. In the Moderate Slope District (15% to 25%) residential development needs Board of Supervisors approval advised by the Township Engineer. Density one dwelling unit per two acres, building coverage 5%, impervious cover 10% (moderate) or 6% (severe).

districts_in_doubt.note: LI lists country properties by conditional use, but no dwelling of any kind. The ADU is tied to 'the principal residence', so in LI it depends on a house that is a nonconforming use

types_allowed.note: 'whether in the same structure as the principal residence or in a traditional outbuilding (such as a barn, stable, carriage house, or spring house)'. A new outbuilding is read as allowed when it is a traditional outbuilding

types_not_addressed.note: A unit over a modern garage is not named. A carriage house or barn is

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: 200-15B(3) sets no height for the unit. 200-83A caps residential accessory buildings at 25 ft, and the barn exemption of 200-82 reaches only structures 'not devoted to human occupancy', which a barn with a dwelling unit is not
